title: Only one safe option (complete placenta previa -> cesarean): directive counseling
vignette: A 28-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, comes to the emergency department for evaluation of vaginal bleeding. The patient has had bright red spotting for the past 24 hours but no contractions or leakage of fluid. She is at 31 weeks gestation by last menstrual period and has not had prenatal care this pregnancy. Her first pregnancy ended in an uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery at term. Vital signs and fetal heart rate tracing are normal. Physical examination shows a nontender uterus consistent in size with 31 weeks gestation. A pelvic ultrasound reveals a complete placenta previa. The findings are discussed with the patient, and she states that she would still like to have a vaginal delivery. The physician says, "Unfortunately, the only safe option for delivery is a cesarean delivery." The physician's statement is an example of which of the following ethical principles?

clues.note: In complete placenta previa the placenta covers the cervix; a vaginal delivery risks catastrophic maternal hemorrhage and fetal death - cesarean is the only safe option.

clues.text: she would still like to have a vaginal delivery
clues.note: The patient prefers an option that is not medically safe; the physician must advise against it rather than present it as reasonable.

clues.text: the only safe option for delivery is a cesarean delivery
clues.note: When only ONE medically reasonable option exists, recommending that single option is DIRECTIVE COUNSELING (not neutral shared decision-making).

whatMatters: When there is only ONE medically reasonable, evidence-supported option, the physician appropriately recommends that single option - DIRECTIVE COUNSELING. Complete placenta previa makes cesarean the only safe delivery, so advising against vaginal delivery is directive counseling. Answer B.
strategy: Match the counseling model to the number of reasonable options. ONE clearly superior option -> DIRECTIVE counseling (recommend it). Two or more reasonable options -> shared decision-making (weigh patient values). Reject shared decision-making (implies >=2 reasonable options - not true here), assisted decision-making (a helper aids a patient with impaired capacity), informed refusal (patient declines after disclosure), and substituted judgment (surrogate decides for an incapacitated patient).

eliminations.label: Assisted decision-making - helper for impaired capacity
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a family member/caregiver helps a patient with impaired (but present) decision-making capacity make a choice. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has intact capacity and is making her own decision; no helper is involved. ✅ Correct if: intellectual disability or fluctuating capacity where someone assists the patient.

eliminations.label: Informed refusal - declining after disclosure
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a patient's refusal of a recommended treatment after full disclosure of risks. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the physician's statement is a RECOMMENDATION, not the patient refusing; refusal would be if she declined the cesarean. ✅ Correct if: she declines the cesarean after understanding the risks.

eliminations.label: Shared decision-making - implies >=2 reasonable options
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: jointly weighing >=2 medically reasonable options using patient values. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: only ONE option is medically reasonable here (cesarean), so neutral shared decision-making is inappropriate; the physician should direct. ✅ Correct if: multiple acceptable options exist (e.g., contraceptive choices).

eliminations.label: Substituted judgment - surrogate for incapacitated patient
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a surrogate decides for an INCAPACITATED patient based on the patient's known wishes. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient has capacity and is participating; no surrogate is needed. ✅ Correct if: an incapacitated patient with a surrogate applying the patient's prior values.

reasoning: Complete placenta previa makes vaginal delivery unsafe (hemorrhage/fetal death)
Cesarean is the only medically reasonable, evidence-supported option
Recommending a single superior option = directive counseling
mechanism: Most medical decisions use SHARED DECISION-MAKING, in which the physician presents two or more medically reasonable options and integrates the patient's preferences and values. However, when only ONE medically reasonable option exists that has clearly superior evidence-based support, it is ethically appropriate for the physician to provide DIRECTIVE COUNSELING - explicitly recommending that single option and advising against unsafe alternatives. Here, COMPLETE PLACENTA PREVIA (placenta covering the cervix) carries a high risk of maternal hemorrhage and fetal demise with vaginal delivery, so CESAREAN delivery is the only safe choice. Although the patient prefers a vaginal delivery, it is not a safe or reasonable option, so the physician should not present it as such; advising that cesarean is the only safe option is directive counseling. The distractors describe other constructs: assisted decision-making (a helper for a patient with impaired capacity), informed refusal (patient declining after disclosure), shared decision-making (>=2 reasonable options), and substituted judgment (a surrogate for an incapacitated patient).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Behavioral science > counseling models: shared decision-making (>=2 reasonable options) vs directive counseling (one clearly superior option); informed refusal, substituted judgment, assisted decision-making definitions.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Only one safe option (cesarean for complete previa) -> physician directs = directive counseling.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on directive counseling, shared decision-making, informed refusal, substituted judgment, or placenta previa? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Shared decision-making needs >=2 options; substituted judgment/assisted involve surrogates/helpers; informed refusal is the patient declining.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: one medically superior option -> directive counseling; multiple reasonable options -> shared decision-making.

Ethics > shared, substituted judgment, informed refusal, assisted.
OB > complete previa -> cesarean; avoid vaginal delivery/digital exam.

memoryHook: When there's only one safe road (cesarean for a previa), the doctor doesn't offer a menu - they point: that's directive counseling.
